clipd — clipboard service

mix --serve <prefix>/lib/clipd/clipd.mix --name clipd runs a clipboard Bus citizen. There is no clipd Rust crate, GUI, Wayland dependency in Mix, or new transport. Store mode holds data in memory. Wayland mode uses the session's external wl-paste and wl-copy executables.

This implementation is not ready for live desktop acceptance: wl-copy cannot advertise a remote lazy offer or run a fetch callback at paste time. Remote password offers and uncached remote types are refused in Wayland mode with LAZY_WAYLAND_UNAVAILABLE. They work lazily through the Bus in store mode. Local Wayland password sets are also refused because wl-copy spools stdin to a temporary file. Observing an existing password offer does not read its content.

Commands

Requests are JSON objects. selection is clipboard (default) or primary. The Rust prototype's primary:true|false alias remains accepted; conflicting aliases are refused. Errors are rc 10 with {error_code,message}. Error messages and service logs never echo request contents.

CommandRequest and reply
clipboard.get{selection?,mime?,offset?,node?} → {mime,data,encoding,size,offset,next_offset,eof,sensitive,stamp} for text; a blob reference for binary/large data
clipboard.set{selection?,mime?,data,encoding?,sensitive?,stamp?} or {selection?,mime,blob} → {applied,stamp?}
clipboard.clear{selection?} → {applied:true}
clipboard.infoBoth selection metadata, node/session, history count, limits, peers and mode
clipboard.historyUp to fifty text previews, newest first: {id,mime,data,size,truncated}
clipboard.pick{index,expected_id?,selection?}; n remains an alias for index
clipboard.push{to,selection?} pushes only to a configured peer key
clipboard.peersConfigured peer map
desktop.clipboard.rotateRestore a history entry
desktop.clipboard.menuPICKER_UNAVAILABLE; use history and indexed pick

clipboard.receive and clipboard.fetch are member-only peer commands. clipboard.observe is a private local watcher callback with a per-process token. clipboard.expire and clipboard.follow are local continuations and refuse Bus dispatch, as do clipboard.cache and clipboard.unpin, which own materialised blob references and release obsolete pins.

clipboard.changed contains metadata only: {node,session,selection,primary,generation,origin_node,origin_session,mime_types, size,sensitive}. A stamp is {origin_node,origin_session,generation}. UUIDs survive process restarts without reusing generations. The last 256 stamps and the current selection fence echoes, independently for both selections.

Small text retains the prototype's UTF-8/base64 reply shape, including byte offsets and eof. Binary/large content uses blobd's existing reference and transfer lane: get returns data:"",encoding:"base64",eof:false,blob:{...}. Call blob.fetch and blob.path rather than advancing next_offset on a blob reply. Set binary data through blob.put followed by clipboard.set {blob}; inline non-text bytes are refused. This is a deliberate difference from the unmerged Rust prototype's binary Bus chunks, required by the blob-only rule.

Wayland blob sets/imports whose bytes are not present return {applied:false,pending:true,stamp}. The existing selection stays usable while blobd fetches. Native blob.fetched/blob.pinned events resume ownership after verified bytes arrive. clipboard.info.pending reports each selection's wait; a later set, clear or external copy cancels the older pending offer.

Mix's Bus-only builtins are clip_get([selection,mime]) and clip_set(text[,selection,mime]). A sole MIME argument remains accepted. clip_get raises for a blob reference. The MCP tools are clipboard_get and clipboard_set, with optional selection and the legacy primary alias.

Configuration and membership

MIXOS_CLIPD_CONFIG selects a schema-1 strict-data file; the default is <etc>/clipboard.conf.mix. Peer keys are exact node names. Nothing is sent outside this configured group. A graphical member has follow:true; server entries default to explicit push/pull. PRIMARY follow requires follow_primary:true at the source. Images are enabled for follow members and require images:true for servers.

{
  schema: 1,
  eager_text_bytes: 1048576,
  history_cap: 50,
  password_timeout: 45,
  follow_primary: false,
  peers: {
    beta: {target:"clipd.beta.example.bus", follow:true},
    archive: {target:"clipd.archive.example.bus", images:false}
  }
}

Configure reciprocal peers. Content APIs admit broker-stamped local callers and configured mesh peers. Membership comes from the broker's broker_peer stamp, never a body field or a client-supplied node claim. A bare service target also admits that broker-stamped local service, for co-located citizens and tests. Use native noded admission and the WireGuard mesh. Missing broker peer stamps fail closed. No scope keys or parallel encryption protocol are introduced.

Follow forwards local changes once; imported changes are not re-exported. Password offers contain metadata only, retain their source and deadline, never enter history or blobd, are fetched on demand, and clear after 45 seconds by default. Store servers do not cache fetched secret bytes. Generation fences refuse stale lazy reads. Replaced or missing sources fail cleanly.

Session integration and external programs

MIXOS_CLIPD_MODE=auto|store|wayland defaults to auto. No display selects store; a display selects Wayland and requires both external tools. Store mode makes no wl-clipboard calls. MIXOS_CLIPD_SESSION identifies the session. The node identity comes from the native node config. Optional config seat selects the Wayland seat through the tools' --seat option.

The desktop role requires wl-paste and wl-copy from wl-clipboard in PATH; the server role needs neither. Both need Mix and noded; binary content also needs blobd. wl-clipboard is an external system package and is not bundled, compiled or linked into MixOS binaries.

Two generation-owned spawn(argv,{exit_event:true}) children run wl-paste [--primary] --watch <prefix>/bin/mix watch.mix <selection>. The callback does not read stdin: it sends a local Bus notification, then closes the pipe. The citizen lists types and reads bounded ordinary text. The KDE password hint is treated conservatively as sensitive whenever present. On-demand reads use wl-paste --type MIME --no-newline, with a five-second deadline and 64 MiB cap; a Mix pipeline helper preserves raw bytes without a temporary read file.

Ordinary sets pass stdin to wl-copy [--primary] --type MIME, which forks and owns the selection. Clears use wl-copy [--primary] --clear. Own eager-text echoes are recognised by exact bytes, because wl-copy cannot add an arbitrary origin marker MIME. Large/binary ownership and multi-MIME preservation need further acceptance: the tool can supply one content payload plus text aliases. The constraint comes from wl-copy's input and ownership path.

clipd@.service reads the graphical session environment; clipd.service is the server store unit. The component installer and release packages ship both units and scripts without enabling them. No desk is restarted by installation of this source change. inputd migrates only the two old clipboard menu/rotate targets from desktop-vt1 to clipd, preserving custom targets and unrelated bindings. This source change does not rewrite a live keymap.

No generic Bus dialog/choice service exists in the current tree. Toolkit dialogs are window-local, and files' chooser is specific to files. A clipboard picker UI remains a follow-up; the service adds no GUI dependency.

Validation

mix services/clipd/tests/clipboard_test.mix checks policy, history, stamps, byte offsets and broker membership. mix services/clipd/tests/clipd_test.mix runs two store citizens against an owned private noded and checks the public API, follow, lazy password fetch, no history, expiry and spoof refusal. It also checks the runtime command list against the registry and uses a real private blobd for binary references and reads outside the Bus.

mix services/clipd/tests/wayland_test.mix starts a private headless compd and checks both selections with the real wl-clipboard tools, own-set echo handling, password history exclusion and expiry. Set MIXOS_TEST_COMPD to a CBC-built binary. The test does not connect to a live desktop.

Before merge: CBC tests for mix and mixos-mcp; a private headless Wayland test; then live VT1/VT3/VT4 and cross-node acceptance by the session owner. The lazy Wayland ownership limitation must be resolved or explicitly scoped before desktop rollout. No gold install, desk restart or merge is authorised here.
